text:
Maria G.: Heads-up: were getting a small flood of tickets where clients see duplicate items after resume. We need to converge SDK semantics for iterator retries + pagination.

Ajay K.: Seen that. Root cause seems to be mismatch in how SDKs treat resume_token vs page commit. Some treat token as next-offset, others as last-seen boundary. Suggest making token opaque and server-authoritative.

Lee T.: Agree with opaque token. Server emits token when it considers a page fully committed. Client treats it as a checkpoint string. SDKs can optionally provide offset helpers but not rely on numeric semantics.

Sophia L.: UX: people like "for await" convenience. If iterator auto-retries, we must guarantee "no-duplicate" yields across resumes. Proposal: iterator persists last_seen_token after yielding page, and dedups items based on token boundaries.

Maria G.: Proposal summary: 1) resume_token = opaque server checkpoint 2) default automatic retries for transient transport errors with sane caps 3) iterator dedups by last_seen_token 4) expose explicit checkpoint()/cursor API for manual control.

Ajay K.: Implementation detail: batching + partial success is tricky. Server should only hand out a resume_token after it has durable-committed that page. If partial writes are possible, token semantics break. We need server-side guarantee or a mapping API.

Lee T.: Transport-wise: keep transport minimal: adapter interface send(req) -> Response | Stream. Let SDK surface own retry/backoff/paging logic so transports (grpc/http/fhttp) stay thin and pluggable.

Sophia L.: Type-level sketch (TS):
```ts
const it = client.listItems({ pageSize: 250, retry: true });
for await (const page of it) {
  // page.items deduped across resumes
}
await it.checkpoint();
```
Make checkpoint() persist last token and allow manual resume later.

Maria G.: Edge-case: what if network dies after server returned token but before client persisted it? Ajay?

Ajay K.: Treat token issuance as authoritative. If client never persisted token, server should reissue same token for same boundary on re-query. That requires server to keep token stable at least for resume window. If tokens rotate short-term, provide translate_token API to map older tokens to current boundaries.

Lee T.: Testing: add cross-language fuzz tests that inject drops at points: after payload send, after payload recv before token ack, mid-page. Ensure resumed iterator never yields duplicates and eventually reaches same commit point.

Sophia L.: Retry defaults: keep simple sane defaults: enabled, maxAttempts=4, baseDelay=50ms, jitter, backoffFactor=2. Expose RetryPolicy object for advanced configs (retryableCodes, maxElapsed). Keep Go defaults slightly more aggressive for low-latency use-cases.

Maria G.: Action items: Sophia to draft API shapes for py/ts/go by EOD Monday. Ajay to propose server commit semantics + token stability window. Lee to PR minimal transport-adapter interface. Ill wire up cross-repo fuzz harness. infra-bot: link to rfc when available. :rocket:

infra-bot: created rfc/2026-sdk-iterator-resume-dedupe-draft
